attacks.claim: S7 does not remove the double-apply seam that divergent-change-0001 is about: after S7 every kit message is still applied twice — once by applyClientMessage(store, ...) and once by propagateToVoiceHost(voiceHost, ...) — so the plan ends with two reducers per message, exactly the shape the finding says must not be left in place.
attacks.evidence: S7's intent only re-targets applyClientMessage's first argument from host.engine to the new ProjectStore; it never removes the propagateToVoiceHost call at apps/server/src/handlers/client-message.ts:513, and S8's deletion list covers the fourteen legacy composition arms only, leaving setKitTransform/setKitGlobal/setHoopConfig/setOutput on both paths. The engine-parity harness (S3) therefore becomes permanent scaffolding rather than a temporary gate.
attacks.repair: Add a step after S7 that makes ONE of the two the sole mutator for kit/output messages: either voiceHost.getProject() is the store (fable's S2 shape) and propagateToVoiceHost is the only reducer, or the store is authoritative and VoiceEngineHost derives its kit from it. Keep engine-parity.test.ts only until that collapse lands, then delete it as scaffolding.

attacks.claim: S7 silently breaks the shared-object-reference invariant that makes today's autosave correct: main.ts constructs both hosts over the SAME project0 object, so VoiceEngineHost's in-place edits are visible to the autosaver; a separate ProjectStore object is not the object voiceHost mutates, so any voice-host-side in-place write (setKitGlobal's reconcileOutputs, setOutput, reloadKit) stops reaching the persisted file.
attacks.evidence: apps/server/src/main.ts:157-163 documents the invariant verbatim: 'Both hosts share the same `project0` object by reference, so the voice host's in-place geometry/routing edits are visible through `host.engine.getProject()` — which is what the autosaver persists.' S7's ProjectStore is constructed independently and S7 never states that voiceHost is re-seeded from store.getProject().
attacks.repair: Construct VoiceEngineHost over store.getProject() (same object identity) and add an assertion to S7's tests that `voiceHost.getProject() === store.getProject()` holds after each mutator, plus after a loadProject/setProject swap — the swap is where identity is actually lost.

attacks.claim: findings_addressed lists duplicated-code-0011 while the plan explicitly refuses to implement it, so the initiative would close with one of its five findings untouched.
attacks.evidence: open_questions entry 5: 'This plan deliberately does NOT include it and recommends it be re-homed to INIT-13-core-surface-trims or shipped standalone', yet findings_addressed[3] = 'duplicated-code-0011'.
attacks.repair: Either drop duplicated-code-0011 from findings_addressed and make the re-homing a Phase 9 ledger decision, or add the 60-LOC math.ts noise consolidation as a leaf step in the last wave (it is file-disjoint from every other step).

attacks.claim: S2 edits apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs but the plan's own verification gate cannot compile Rust, so the desktop shell change lands unverified by `pnpm gates`.
attacks.evidence: package.json:22-23 — `gates` = `with-gate-lock.mjs pnpm run gates:run`, and `gates:run` = `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`. No cargo/tauri build participates. S2's live-path proof only boots the Node server, never the desktop shell.
attacks.repair: Add `cargo check --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (or `pnpm --filter @ledrums/desktop build`) to S2's verification, and confirm the deleted `.env(...)` block sets nothing else that the shell depends on.

attacks.claim: S6 creates a second verbatim copy of Engine's 23 mutators inside packages/core and leaves BOTH copies live for four waves, and no test compares them — engine-parity.test.ts compares legacy-vs-voice, never Engine-vs-ProjectStore, so a transcription slip in the copy is caught only by hand-mirrored assertions written by the same implementer.
attacks.evidence: S6 intent: 'carrying VERBATIM copies of Engine's mutator section (engine.ts:250-437)'; S6 verification mirrors engine.test.ts assertions rather than differentially driving both objects. S9 (the deletion of the original) is four waves later.
attacks.repair: Make S6's test differential rather than mirrored: drive the same generated message stream through `new Engine(pA)` and `new ProjectStore(pB)` and assert deep-equal Projects — the same technique S3 already uses for the other pair, reusing its message table.

attacks.claim: S13 changes what the offline preview renders while apps/web has no pixel-level test for the preview at all, so the step's acceptance bar rests on a human eyeballing two screenshots.
attacks.evidence: Verified against source: core caps the pool at 256 slots (packages/core/src/voice/voice-pool.ts:15) where sim's array is unbounded, and mix-input seeds change from apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/sim.ts:496 `(seed ^ Math.imul(index+1, 0x9e3779b9))` to packages/core/src/voice/voice-pool.ts:172 `deriveSeed(slot.seed, index + 1)`.
attacks.plan_response: S13's verification names exactly these three deltas ('the preview gains core's 256-voice cap', canvas-scene resolution, 'mix-input seeds change from sim's seed ^ Math.imul(index+1, 0x9e3779b9) to core's deriveSeed') and gives each its own pinning assertion; behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps (1) states plainly that render.ts has no test file and that the screenshot comparison is weaker than an assertion, which is why S13 lands alone in its wave with a single-file revert.

attacks.claim: S8 deletes fourteen reducer arms while packages/protocol still decodes those messages, so a client sending one gets a silent no-op — the same silent-drop class this initiative exists to remove.
attacks.evidence: S8's file list contains no protocol package file, so the ClientMessage union keeps the fourteen variants. I confirmed the premise that nothing in-repo sends them: grep across apps/web/src returns 0 hits for setParam/addLayer/addClip/setBinding/setActiveSection and the rest (only setTransport, 4 hits, survives).
attacks.plan_response: S8's verification requires it explicitly before the deletion: 'confirm packages/protocol still accepts them (a message the server now ignores must be a decode-level rejection or an explicit no-op, never a silent drop) — if any arm is still reachable, keep it on ProjectStore instead of deleting it.'

required_repairs: Collapse to a single reducer per kit/output message after S7 — the plan currently leaves applyClientMessage and propagateToVoiceHost both live, so the finding's mechanism survives the initiative.
Preserve (and assert) project-object identity between ProjectStore and VoiceEngineHost, or the autosaver stops seeing voice-host in-place edits (main.ts:157-163 invariant).
Reconcile findings_addressed with the plan body: either implement duplicated-code-0011 as a leaf step or drop it from the list.
Add a Rust build check to S2's verification — `pnpm gates` is typecheck+test only and cannot compile the src-tauri edit.
Make S6's ProjectStore test differential against Engine rather than a hand-mirrored copy of engine.test.ts's assertions.

attacks.claim: S8's acceptance bar — swap Sim's lifecycle for a full core RenderEngine and have all 14 sim suites pass UNMODIFIED — is provably unattainable, and the step names no expected deltas, no golden fixture and no fallback, so it cannot be repaired by editing a step; it needs the deltas designed in.
attacks.evidence: Core's pool is fixed at 256 slots with oldest-releasing-first stealing (packages/core/src/voice/voice-pool.ts:15,83-101) where Sim's array is unbounded, and mix-input seeds differ concretely: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/sim.ts:496 `(seed ^ Math.imul(index+1, 0x9e3779b9))` vs packages/core/src/voice/voice-pool.ts:172 `deriveSeed(slot.seed, index+1)`. S8 also swaps the whole engine (not just the pool), so the surface of change is strictly larger. S8's verification states any failure 'identifies a semantic gap ... not a test needing an update' — leaving the step with no green path.
attacks.repair: Split S8 into pool-adoption then envelope-tick adoption, enumerate the behaviour deltas (voice cap, canvas-scene resolution, mix-input seed derivation) as pinned assertions, and capture a pre-change golden fixture of per-frame voice tuples to replay — i.e. the shape the opus variant's S13/S14 use.

attacks.claim: S7 deletes packages/core/src/engine/transport.ts, which the LIVE voice loop imports — the step cannot land green and the summary's end-state ('framebuffer.ts + render-context.ts survive') is factually wrong.

attacks.repair: Keep engine/transport.ts (and its barrel export) out of the deletion set, as the opus variant's S9 does; optionally relocate it to a render/ directory in a separate mechanical step.

attacks.claim: The plan's only blocks_execution question is built on a false premise: LayersDock.svelte does not author Project.composition.layers/clips and sends none of the legacy reducer messages, so the initiative would stall waiting on a decision about a dock that does not do what the plan says it does.
attacks.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/app/docks/LayersDock.svelte contains only bus/voice controls — store.setPolyphony, store.stopBus, store.setCrossfade, store.busLevelsDisplay — with zero ws sends. grep across apps/web/src for the fourteen discriminants ('setParam','setLayer','addLayer','removeLayer','addClip','removeClip','setActiveSection','setBinding','removeBinding','addSong','removeSong','addSection','removeSection','setSectionLayerClip') returns 0 hits each; only setTransport appears (4 hits).

attacks.repair: Add VoiceEngineHost.setTransport (writing composition.transport, which its loop at voice-engine-host.ts:483 already reads) and an explicit adopt/setProject path for loadProject, and name legacy-content.ts's caller and target object in S5.

attacks.claim: S6's verification asks for a grep over src-tauri returning zero LEDRUMS_ENGINE hits, but no step in the plan edits src-tauri/lib.rs, so the check can never pass.

attacks.repair: Re-rate: S2/S3 low-to-medium (both fully covered by per-pixel determinism suites), S8/S9 high — and put S8 alone in its own wave with a single-file revert.

attacks.claim: S7 claims all existing sim suites pass UNMODIFIED after adopting core VoicePool; that is not achievable, because adopting the pool changes at least the voice cap and the mix-input seed derivation.

attacks.claim: S2 re-points the authoritative store onto voiceHost while both hosts currently share one Project object by reference, so the step risks losing the invariant that keeps autosave correct.
attacks.evidence: apps/server/src/main.ts:157-163 documents the shared-reference invariant explicitly, and notes that references split after the first loadProject/adoptPatch.
